source_user: A service receives a mix of short prompts and long generations. Design an evaluation plan that reports TTFT, TPOT, throughput, queueing, and P99 latency. Scenario variant 81: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: separate prefill and decode behavior; fix workload distribution; report warmup; use repeated trials; capture GPU memory and request-level traces.
corrected_answer: For scenario variant 81: Freeze and record the model/tokenizer, runtime and kernel versions, hardware topology, precision, parallelism, scheduler and batching policy, sampling settings, arrival process, prompt/output-length distributions, offered-load points, concurrency, SLOs, and correctness criteria; conclusions apply only to this configuration. Hypothesis: at each prespecified offered load, candidate B changes paired TTFT, TPOT, queue wait, throughput, and P99 latency versus baseline A by a predefined practically meaningful effect in steady state, without unacceptable correctness, timeout, cancellation, or error-rate regression. Pre-register the effect threshold, confidence/uncertainty rule, sample size or stopping rule, exclusions, and missing-data treatment. Replay the same fixed, stratified request trace with randomized A/B order and repeated independent time blocks on equivalent isolated hosts; discard only a documented warm-up. Capture admission, queue entry/exit, dispatch, prefill start/end, first-token, each decode-token, completion, cancellation, timeout, retry, error, and rejection timestamps. Report queue-inclusive and compute-only TTFT, TPOT with its exact token/time denominator, end-to-end latency, request and token throughput, queue depth/wait, saturation, and P50/P95/P99/P99.9, stratified by prompt length, output length, concurrency, and load. Also record GPU memory allocated/reserved/peak, KV-cache occupancy and evictions, utilization, power/thermal state, CPU/RAM, network, OOMs, throttling, and runtime errors; verify output correctness and count all requests in denominators. Analyze paired deltas with confidence intervals and report variability and exclusions. Confounders include host drift, thermal throttling, cache state, background work, request-order effects, tokenizer differences, retries, and workload drift; randomize or block on these and retain raw request-level traces. Stop or roll back if correctness, error, OOM, timeout, or agreed tail-latency/SLO guardrails regress beyond their predeclared limits. Do not infer capacity or causality outside the tested hardware, software, workload, load range, and replication; domain-expert review and an independent rerun are evidence required for a deployment decision.
